title: Trying to find edge in 2026 with a bot made by claude fable 5
author: Impressive-Badger412
selftext:
I’ve been building trading bots and researching market inefficiencies for a while. I’m curious about your opinion: do you think it’s still realistic for an independent developer to find a sustainable edge in 2026?    
I’m talking about any market: prediction markets (Polymarket, Limitless), sports betting, crypto, traditional exchanges, arbitrage, market making, etc.    
Are markets now so efficient that it’s nearly impossible, or do you think there are still opportunities if you look in the right places?    
Where would you focus your time today, and what areas would you avoid?

comments.author: epicskyes
comments.body: There’s always an edge to exploit.  What exactly that edge  is would determine how long it stays sharp.

comments.author: CryptographerBig7624
comments.body:
The "is there still an edge" framing is where people trip up imo. It's not yes or no — it's that the kind of edge a solo dev can get has changed.

You're not gonna beat a market maker on speed or find a clean arb that survives real fills. That's gone for independents. But that was never where retail edge lived anyway.

What's left is mostly execution and risk, not prediction. Half the "no edge" conclusions are really just random entries plus sloppy sizing. A mediocre signal with disciplined exits beats a good signal traded emotionally, and that gap is yours to take. Same with regime — you don't need edge in every condition, you need to know which conditions your thing works in and sit out the rest. Most break-even systems are one good regime averaged with one bad one.

What I'd avoid is anything where the edge is supposed to come from the LLM predicting. Claude's great for building and analyzing, useless as an oracle. Use it to kill bad ideas faster, not to generate alpha.

Not financial advice, just where I'd put my time if I started today.

comments.author: Unfair_Yogurt8597
comments.body: sports betting is probably one of the easiest to find an edge in, the problem is the betting platforms limiting and banning your account once they realize you have. I had to stop sports betting last year after having all my accounts limited/soft banned and not wanting to go through the hassle of using a friend or family member's account due to taxes.

comments.author: Betamigos
comments.body: Honest take: yes, edge still exists in 2026, but it's thinner and more perishable, so the game is speed and measurement, not clever models. In sports specifically the money is in catching soft lines before they move and then proving you're actually beating the close. Closing line value over a big sample is the only signal that separates real edge from variance, so build your logging around that from day one or you'll fool yourself for months. Full disclosure, I built Betamigos (betamigos.io) for exactly this on the sports side (odds-drop alerts in seconds plus auto CLV tracking), so I'm biased, but even if you roll your own, make bet-price-vs-close your north star metric.
